sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Hampton University and Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University (FAMU) differ in several key aspects. Hampton is a private nonprofit institution located in Hampton, with an undergraduate enrollment of 3,727 students. In contrast, FAMU is a public university situated in Tallahassee, serving 7,582 undergraduates. Tuition costs also vary significantly between the two, with Hampton charging $30,592 for in-state students, while FAMU's in-state tuition is $5,785. These differences highlight the distinct nature of Hampton vs FAMU in terms of ownership, size, location, and cost.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing the cost of attendance between Hampton University and Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University (FAMU), there are notable differences. Hampton University, a private institution, charges $30,592 for both in-state and out-of-state tuition. In contrast, FAMU, a public university, has a significantly lower in-state tuition of $5,785 and an out-of-state tuition of $17,725. Regarding student debt, the median debt for completers at Hampton is $25,442, while at FAMU it is slightly lower at $23,548. These figures illustrate the financial considerations prospective students must evaluate when choosing between Hampton vs FAMU.
